Based on the provided context, the answer is **no**, you will not be able to exercise options that were granted after your employment ended, because the context does not support the premise that you would receive a new stock grant after termination.

Here is the breakdown based on the text:

1.  **Vesting requires employment:** The "Option Vesting" section states that "Vesting means that you have to remain employed by, or are otherwise a service provider to, GitLab for a certain period of time before you can fully own the stock." It further clarifies that if you leave before the vesting period is complete, "none of your options will be vested."
2.  **Exercise window applies to *vested* options:** The "Exercise Window After Termination" section states that if your employment ends, you have a three-month window to exercise your **vested** options. It does not mention exercising unvested options or options granted post-termination.
3.  **No provision for post-termination grants:** The context does not contain any policy stating that new stock grants are issued after employment ends. Typically, stock grants are issued to current employees or service providers as part of compensation. Since you are no longer employed, you would not be eligible for new grants, and therefore would not have any new vested options to exercise within the 90-day window.

Additionally, the context notes that policies may vary by location ("applied in accordance with applicable local laws"), but it does not provide specific UK exceptions that would allow for post-termination grants or the exercise of unvested options. Therefore, based strictly on the provided text, you cannot exercise options from a grant received after employment ends because such a grant would not exist under standard policy.

Use the following context to answer the question.

Context:
[Equity Compensation > About Your Ownership in GitLab > Questions about your stock plan or retail account > Exercise Window After Termination]
If your employment ends for whatever reason, you have a three month window to exercise your vested options, or lose them. During this window you would have to pay the exercise price and in some cases the tax on the gain in value of your stock options, which could be considerable.

[Leave Types > GitLab Parental Leave > Equity Vesting During Leave]
Stock vesting is paused after six months of continuous leave and resumes on your first day back at work. Please note that this policy is applied in accordance with applicable local laws and statutory requirements, and may not apply in all locations or to all types of leave globally.

For complete details, please refer to our [Equity policy page](/handbook/total-rewards/stock-options/#equity-policies). If you have questions or concerns about how this applies to your specific situation, please submit a [Compass ticket](https://app.serval.com/new-request) to the Stock Admin team directly.

[Equity Compensation > About Your Ownership in GitLab > Option Vesting]
Vesting means that you have to remain employed by, or are otherwise a service provider to, GitLab for a certain period of time before you can fully own the stock under your stock option grant. Instead of giving you the right to purchase and own all of the common stock under your stock option on day one, you get to own the stock under your stock option in increments over time. This process is called vesting and different companies offer vesting schedules of different lengths. At GitLab, our standard practice is to issue options with a four year vesting schedule so you would own a quarter of your stock after 12 months, half of your stock after two years, and all of it after 4 years. Vesting happens on a monthly basis after the first year for new hire grants and monthly after grant for refresh grants. A cliff on a new hire grant is the period at the beginning of the vesting period where your equity does not vest monthly, but instead vests at the end of the cliff period. At most companies, including GitLab, this cliff period is generally one year. This means that if you leave your job either voluntarily or involuntarily before you've worked for a whole year, none of your options will be vested. At the end of that year, you'll vest the entire year's worth (12 months) of equity all at once. This helps keep the ownership of GitLab stock to team members who have worked at the company for a meaningful amount of time.

Question: In the United Kingdom, if I receive a stock grant after my employment has already ended, will I still be able to exercise my options within the standard 90‑day window?
